text:
michael: Heads-up: Support reported tenant 'blink' saw v2 badge in Console but routing traces show a mix of v1/v2 for the same session. This is creating weird quota churn. anyone seen late-arriving router events cause attribution flips?

tara: yes, we saw similar when router does async fallback. incoming event (fastpath) is emitted immediately for dashboards, router decision comes later. console currently attributes by whichever event arrives first.

michael: example trace: 
```
incoming 10:12:01 req=aa11 header=X-API-Version=v2
fastpath.metric 10:12:01 req=aa11 badge=v2
router.decision 10:12:04 req=aa11 model=redwood-v1 reason=fallback_len
exec.finish 10:12:05 req=aa11 model=redwood-v1 tokens=312
billing.emit 10:12:05 req=aa11 billed_tag=client:v2
```
so console shows badge=v2 but router/execution = v1.

leo: long-term fix: unify attribution on a single canonical field that is set after routing/execution, e.g., resolved_model or attributed_model. short-term: add an "attribution_confidence" score and a trust-window heuristic.

sophia: how does attribution_confidence work?

leo: idea: compute confidence by looking at event provenance. if attributed_model comes from exec.finish (post-run) confidence=1.0. if from initial header only and no exec event within 10s, confidence=0.3. if we have both header and routed_model but they differ, compute: confidence = 0.7 for routed_model, 0.2 for header. We can expose this as a numeric on console and use it for automated reconciliation.

tara: implementation notes: pipeline already has three streams: fastpath (pre-route), route_events, exec_events. We need to join by req_id with a max window ~12s to attach exec/resolved fields to the fastpath record. This will add memory footprint; we'll keep join keyed by tenant and shard.

michael: UX: Console should show "version badge (attribution_confidence=0.72)" and allow filtering to only show counts where confidence >= 0.8. That reduces noise.

sophia: billing must be careful. we can't flip invoices without ops/legal. but we can run a dry reconciliation: compute new attribution using precedence exec.resolved_model > router.model > billing.billed_tag > header. produce delta report.

leo: reconciliation output format proposal: CSV with columns [tenant, window_start, old_tokens, new_tokens, delta_tokens, pct_delta, top_example_req_ids]. include small sample traces for each tenant to help debugging.

michael: add a "silent-correct" policy: if pct_delta < 0.5% or est_delta_dollars < $10, mark as silent-correct and schedule a background invoice patch with audit trail; otherwise surface to revenue-ops and tenant. legal approves silent corrections under threshold.

tara: for rollout: 1) emit resolved_model into events (nullable) 2) start shadow join for 24h and compute diffs 3) surface UI confidence and cohort toggle 4) run reconciliation dry-run and produce CSVs 5) decide writeback policy.

sophia: monitoring: add alert if any tenant has rolling mismatch rate > 2% for 30m. also alert if join-latency p99 > 12s.

audit-bot: ticket created: BILL-1322 "late-join-attribution-reconciliation" assigned to @michael and @tara (https://redwood.internal/tickets/BILL-1322).

michael: i'll draft the Console copy: "Attribution shows model we believe executed. Confidence < 0.5 indicates preliminary data and counts may be recalculated." will include link to /docs/attribution-latejoin.md.

leo: tech perf: run perf sim at 60k rps with 8% fallback and 2% delayed router events; validate memory and p99 join latency.

tara: i'll schedule perf sim for tomorrow and open the PR for resolved_model field today. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
